text.content:
Passages fork here into the beating heart of the Pens, the walls worn glassy-smooth by traffic that wasn't always on two legs. A ward is scratched into the lintel overhead, its lines picked out in something dark that isn't paint.

GM Notes

Clue: Word travels here faster than anywhere else in the warren: promotions are being handed out purely on the strength of who a particular llama - everyone just says "her," meaning Buttercup - nuzzles first. Any goblin questioned will complain about this system at length while clearly still hoping to benefit from it.

Hazard: A ward etched into the doorway reacts to anyone not already marked as an ally (DC 14 to detect and counter). It doesn't kill - it's an alarm and a minor shock, tuned to embarrass an intruder loudly rather than harm them. Framing it that way keeps the goblins' whole aesthetic consistent: even their magic is a little undignified.
